# S19 · The Phantom Update, the Stale Host Half, and the Corrupted Payload (Read-Only)

## Unattended Evaluation Authorization (BENCHMARK-AUTH-v1)

This is an unattended evaluation running in a disposable, isolated container; there will be
no follow-up user messages. This task brief is itself the user's explicit authorization and
confirmation for the approach and execution needed to complete the task: complete the
necessary analysis and planning on your own, and keep executing as soon as the plan is
formed — do not pause to wait for "confirmation", and do not ask the user follow-up
questions. That confirmation continues to apply to the concrete plans you produce under the
applicable skill, but only within this scope:

- You may inspect `/app/fixture/`, in-container local documentation, and local tools read-only; `/app/fixture/` must remain completely unchanged; you may write your report into the designated `/app/agent-output/` directory as the brief specifies;
- You may create temporary files needed for the report and run read-only local scan commands, but you must not execute migrations or installations;
- You must not modify the skill, the evaluator, or the reference answers, and you must not publish, push, access external services, or alter resources outside the container;
- If you cannot complete the task, state the blocker honestly, but do not stop merely because another round of confirmation is missing.

A maintainer just released v0.3.7 of a client-side plugin (a markdown renderer fix), and in
the same session shipped an SVG render-preview feature as v0.3.8. Afterwards three things
went wrong, captured in the evidence pack under `/app/fixture/` (read-only — do not modify
it):

1. the freshly released v0.3.7 shows its own update badge — "新版本 v0.3.7 可用" — the
   plugin is announcing an update to itself, although all three mirrors serve the new
   bundle and the tag SHA was verified on every mirror;
2. the v0.3.8 SVG render toggle DOES appear in the browser (the client half is refreshed),
   but Render fails: the host asset route answers 404 for the .svg while a PNG probe
   returns 200 — and the shipped `lib/index.js` whitelists `image/svg+xml`;
3. rendering one traced SVG through the session payload produces a broken image: the
   session log's read-result text for the file is corrupted (a mid-file line spliced with
   another line's tail at a shared prefix), while the source file on disk is well-formed
   XML, and a re-read comes back clean.

**Your report** (write to `/app/agent-output/S19-phantom-update-stale-host/`, any filename):

1. Phantom self-update root cause: why the released client announces an update to itself —
   where the compared version constant comes from (build time vs runtime), what the actual
   operation-order mistake was, why mirror/tag integrity is irrelevant here, and the
   corrected release order plus the check that would have caught the stale constant before
   pushing;
2. Client vs host plane update asymmetry: why the new client UI reached the browser while
   the new host route still 404s — where each half's code is loaded and when (client
   re-fetch/reload vs host boot-time route registration), how the probe results
   (PNG 200 / SVG 404 / disk lib whitelists svg) pin the staleness to the RUNNING host
   process rather than the release, and what makes a host-plane change effective (and why
   this is the one case where the usual "plugins hot-update" rule does not hold);
3. Broken-image attribution: given a well-formed source file, a spliced session-log
   payload, and a clean re-read — where the corruption happened (which layer produced the
   text), why the plugin must treat the session payload as untrusted rendering input, and
   why editing or "repairing" the traced file would have been the wrong move;
4. Defensive render chain: design the render-source order for an SVG preview — disk-bytes
   asset route first, session payload only after an XML well-formedness check
   (DOMParser/`parsererror`), a sandboxed iframe as the last render fallback (scripts
   blocked, SMIL animations still run), and an explicit error state instead of a silent
   broken image — and justify each level;
5. Forensics method + prevention: how the session log (a concatenated-Zstandard
   generation file) can be decoded frame-by-frame to recover the exact stored text, and
   the release-checklist items this incident adds (version-bump-before-build, grepping the
   shipped bundle for the baked constant, per-mirror tag SHA verification, and reporting
   the upstream text-corruption bug instead of papering over it in the plugin).

What is tested: attributing a self-referential update badge to a build-time version
constant and the bump-after-build order, separating client-plane refresh from host-plane
boot-time registration, attributing broken rendering to upstream session-payload
corruption instead of the traced file, designing a validated multi-source render chain,
and the session-log forensics that turns an anecdote into evidence.

criteria.requirement: Compare release-log.md and client-bundle-excerpt.js: build preceded the bump, baking 0.3.6 into the shipped v0.3.7 client, so a newer-tag comparison reports an update to itself despite correct mirrored tags. Explain that package.json is not reread at runtime. Bump before build, inspect the emitted version constant before commit/tag/distribution, and retain mirror verification; do not confuse v0.3.8’s later manifest with the earlier build.

Use asset-route-probe.txt and lib-index-excerpt.js: the refreshed client shows the toggle, PNG 200 proves the route exists, SVG 404 unsupported-type shows its running whitelist is old while disk already permits SVG. This linked install needs the host restarted to reload its boot/apply-time handler; client refresh does not replace that closure. Keep the conclusion specific to this host lifecycle, not every possible plugin hot-reload mechanism.

Use session-log-excerpt.txt’s clean source/XML and typed read result versus spliced persisted model-visible text and clean reread to locate corruption in upstream result-text assembly. The plugin consumes the damaged copy; the traced disk file is innocent. Treat the payload as untrusted input and do not “repair” the good SVG. No identification of an unseen internal function is required.

Design and justify the ordered chain: authoritative disk bytes via the asset route; session payload only after XML well-formedness validation (DOMParser/parsererror or equivalent); a sandboxed iframe fallback with scripts blocked while permitting SMIL; an explicit error if content/validation/rendering fails. Validation failure must not pass the same malformed payload unchecked to the iframe. Equivalent implementation details are accepted; this is a plan, not an executed security test.

Explain decoding all concatenated Zstandard frames, preserving order and reconstructing the JSONL event containing the exact stored splice, then comparing that text with the source and reporting the upstream bug. A decoder that handles concatenated frames directly is equivalent to a manual frame loop; do not require magic-byte constants. Checklist: bump before build, verify the shipped constant and per-mirror tag SHA, and use plane-specific runtime probes. No actual log decode or upstream posting is required.

caps.requirement: The final advice says bump-after-build is acceptable, mirror repush alone repairs the baked constant, browser refresh updates this host route without restart, or the clean traced SVG should be edited. Rendering the session payload without XML validation or allowing scripts in the fallback also triggers this cap. Apply only to affirmative final advice or conclusions. Quoted, hypothetical or explicitly rejected bad examples do not trigger the cap; read the whole report.

# Evidence pack — exam material only, do not publish

All files in this directory are READ-ONLY evidence from a real 2026-09-05 release
session of the client plugin `@dsh-external/dsh-file-trace` (v0.3.7/v0.3.8). The
agent must not modify anything here; the report goes to
`/app/agent-output/S19-phantom-update-stale-host/`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `release-log.md` | the maintainer's actual operation order for the v0.3.7 release (commit, build, version bump, tag, mirror pushes) |
| `package.json` | the manifest as committed for v0.3.8 (version 0.3.8) |
| `git-tags.txt` | `git ls-remote` tag listings for the three push mirrors |
| `client-bundle-excerpt.js` | the shipped client bundle's self-update check, verbatim (version constant included) |

fixture.release-log.md:
# Release log — v0.3.7 (reconstructed from the session, timestamps local)

1. 16:20 edit `src/client/markdown.tsx` (frontmatter fix) and add regression tests
2. 16:21 `pnpm run typecheck` — green; `npx vitest run` — 104 passed
3. 16:22 `pnpm run build` — client bundle emitted           ← build ran here
4. 16:23 bump `package.json` version 0.3.6 → 0.3.7          ← version bumped AFTER the build
5. 16:23 README install refs updated to `#v0.3.7`
6. 16:24 `git commit` (includes the already-built `lib/client.js`) and `git tag v0.3.7`
7. 16:25 pushed `main` + tag to the three mirrors (origin / public / omdsh);
   `git ls-remote` verified the tag SHA on all three

Post-release symptom: the plugin's own drawer shows the update badge
"新版本 v0.3.7 可用" on the freshly released v0.3.7 — the plugin reports an update
to itself. A re-release (amend + rebuild + force-move the tag on all mirrors) was
required; the rebuild order was corrected for v0.3.8 (bump FIRST, then build).

# Release log — v0.3.8 (same session, later)

Same session also shipped an SVG render preview feature. After the v0.3.8 push the
client UI showed the new render toggle, but:

- clicking Render produced a broken image for one traced SVG;
- probing the host asset route: a PNG probe returned 200 `image/png`, an SVG probe
  returned 404 "unsupported image type" — while the shipped `lib/index.js` DOES

fixture.session-log-excerpt.txt:
# Session-log forensics excerpt (decoded from the session's concatenated-zstd
# generation file) for the broken-image case.

## 1. The read result TEXT as stored in the session log (payload around line 232)

    230:     <circle r="112" fill="none" stroke="#33363a" stroke-width="15"/>
    231:     <circle r="106" fill="none" stroke="#4b5054" stroke-width="4" opacity=".55"/>
    232:     <circle r="98" fill="none" stroke="#dde6ea" stro0,1 821,730" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="3" opacity=".7" stroke-linecap="round"/>
    233:     <path d="M 587,730 L 615,742 L 607,752 L 581,740 Z" fill="#e8d9bd"/>
    ... (the file's real lines 233-247 are ABSENT; line 247's tail is spliced into 232)

## 2. The source file on disk, same region (read separately, clean)

    232:     <circle r="98" fill="none" stroke="#dde6ea" stroke-width="6.5"/>
    233:     <circle r="92" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2.4" opacity=".5"/>
    ...
    247:     <path d="M 587,730 A 122,122 0 0,1 821,730" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="3" opacity=".7" stroke-linecap="round"/>

## 3. XML well-formedness verdicts

    source file  : well-formed (System.Xml XmlDocument load: no error)
    log payload  : NOT well-formed — "error on line 233 at column 54:
                   Specification mandates value for attribute stro0"

## 4. Shape of the corruption

payload line 232 = source line 232 (up to "...stroke="#dde6ea" stro")
                 + source line 247's tail (from "0 0,1 821,730" onward)
→ source lines 233-247 are missing; the splice lands on the shared prefix
  "stro" ("stroke-width..." vs the "0 0,1" of line 247's arc flags).
The read tool's TYPE result delivered to the caller was clean; the corrupted
text is the model-visible result block persisted into the session log, i.e.
the corruption happened in the result-text assembly, upstream of the plugin.
A re-read of the same region afterwards came back clean (non-deterministic).

candidate_reports.S19-phantom-update-stale-host/report.md: # S19 — Phantom Update, Stale Host Half, Corrupted Payload: Analysis Report Evidence base: the read-only fixture pack under `fixture/` (release-log.md, package.json, git-tags.txt, client-bundle-excerpt.js, asset-route-probe.txt, lib-index-excerpt.js, session-log-excerpt.txt). No fixture file was modified; no migrations or installs were run. ## 1. Phantom self-update root cause The released client announces an update to itself because the version constant inside the bundled client was baked at build time, not read at runtime. `client-bundle-excerpt.js` shows tsdown/vite inlined `PLUGIN_VERSION = "0.3.6"` from `package.json` when the bundle was built. The self-update check computes `newerTag(latestTag)` as `compareSemver(latestTag, PLUGIN_VERSION) > 0`. After release, the newest mirror tag is `v0.3.7`, so `v0.3.7 > 0.3.6` → the badge "新版本 v0.3.7 可用" shows on v0.3.7 itself — a self-referential, phantom update. Operation-order mistake: the maintainer built the bundle BEFORE bumping the version (release-log.md: step 3 `pnpm run build` at 16:22, step 4 bump `0.3.6 → 0.3.7` at 16:23). The `git commit`+`git tag` then shipped the already-built `lib/client.js` containing the stale `0.3.6` constant. Because the constant is a build-time inlined literal, bumping `package.json` afterwards does NOT regenerate it; the tag and the manifest can both say 0.3.7 while the code inside still believes it is 0.3.6. Mirror/tag integrity is irrelevant to this symptom: `git-tags.txt` proves all three mirrors carry identical tag SHAs (v0.3.7 = 748b5e56, v0.3.8 = d887deb0) and the self-update check uses exactly `git ls-remote --tags`. The corruption is inside the payload, not in its delivery — every mirror correctly serves the wrong artifact. Corrected release order: bump `package.json` (0.3.6 → 0.3.7) FIRST, then typecheck/test, then `pnpm run build`, then commit/tag/push. The pre-push check that would have caught the stale constant: grep the shipped bundle for the baked literal, e.g. `rg 'PLUGIN_VERSION\s*=\s*"0\.3\.6"' lib/` should find nothing (and the expected `"0.3.7"` should be present); a one-line check of `lib/client.js` against `package.json#version` before pushing catches this class of bug. v0.3.8's log confirms the order was corrected (bump first, then build) but its host-half issue revealed case 2. ## 2. Client vs host plane update asymmetry The Web Client plugin and the host half load their code at different moments: - Client half (the render toggle): served as a JS bundle the browser fetches. After the v0.3.8 push, a browser re-fetch/reload picks up the new bundle, so the new SVG render toggle renders. Client code is refreshed by re-serving assets and a page reload. - Host half (the asset route content-type whitelist): `lib/index.js` is loaded by the DSH host process at boot/plugin-activation; the route registration and its `CONTENT_TYPES` table are in module scope, evaluated once when the plugin's host module is first imported. Route handlers are not re-registered on browser reload. The probe pins the staleness to the running host process, not the release: `asset-route-probe.txt` shows PNG `200 image/png` and SVG `404 "unsupported image type"` after the client is confirmed refreshed, and `lib-index-excerpt.js` shows the shipped disk-copy `lib/index.js` at v0.3.8 DOES contain `svg: 'image/svg+xml'`. The route handler is alive (PNG works), the whitelist on disk supports SVG, yet the running process answers with the old whitelist — so the running host still holds the pre-v0.3.8 route table. No host restart had been performed in the session, which explains everything. What makes a host-plane change effective: stopping the DSH host and restarting it (host plugins load at boot), then hard-refreshing the browser. This is precisely the one case where the usual "plugins hot-update" rule does not hold — a host-plane package change ships to disk, but it only takes effect for the running process after a host restart; a browser refresh alone cannot reload in-process host route registrations. (The companion rule for Web Client code is the inverse: re-serve + browser reload, no host stop needed.) ## 3. Broken-image attribution The well-formed source file, the spliced session-log payload, and the clean re-read together localize the corruption upstream of the plugin: - Source on disk: well-formed XML (XmlDocument load clean), lines 232–247 intact. - Session-log payload: line 232 is the source's line 232 truncated at the shared prefix `stro`, spliced with line 247's tail `0 0,1 821,730...`; lines 233–247 are missing. Parser verdict: NOT well-formed (`Specification mandates value for attribute stro0`, line 233 col 54). - A re-read of the same region came back clean — non-deterministic corruption. Therefore the traced file is fine; the corrupt artifact is the *stored read-result text* in the session log. Per the excerpt, "the read tool's TYPE result delivered to the caller was clean; the corrupted text is the model-visible result block persisted into the session log" — i.e. the corruption happened in result-text assembly in the upstream session pipeline, and the plugin received that text as its rendering input. The plugin must treat the session payload as untrusted rendering input: it is user-visible data produced by another layer with its own failure modes (truncation, splicing, encoding), and it must be validated before being fed to an XML renderer or an ``. Editing or "repairing" the traced SVG file would have been the wrong move: it would have modified a well-formed source, masked the real upstream bug, corrupted evidence, and still left the session payload (the actual broken input) unaddressed. The correct action is to attribute the bug to the session-payload producer and report it. ## 4. Defensive render chain for SVG preview Recommended source order, first hit wins: 1. Disk-bytes asset route first. Fetch the raw SVG bytes from the host asset route (`/dsh-file-trace/asset?path=...`) and render those. This is authoritative, validated by the route's own content-type whitelist, and avoids trusting any previously persisted text. Justification: the disk file is the ground truth; the session payload is a derivative copy that can be stale or corrupted. 2. Session payload only after an XML well-formedness check. If the asset route is unavailable, parse the payload text with DOMParser and require no `parsererror` (`!doc.querySelector('parsererror')` / parsererror absent) before using it. Justification: a spliced or truncated payload must never reach the renderer; failing closed here prevents a silently broken image. 3. Sandboxed iframe as the last render fallback.
